## Cumulative frequency histogram {#l2-cumulative-graphs }

- Cumulative frequencies never decrease.
- The final height is the total number of observations.
- Each bar shows the total counted **up to that value or class**.
- Use **cumulative frequency** on the vertical axis.
- Keep a **half-column gap before the first bar**, as for the ordinary histogram.


::: {.takeaway}
Ordinary frequency asks “how many here?” Cumulative frequency asks “how many so far?”
:::
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 45 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
CambridgeMATHS NSW Stage 6 Mathematics Extension 1 Year 11 (second edition), p. 615, uses the same bar positioning for cumulative and ordinary histograms. Keep the leading half-column gap; adjacent bars still touch.

For intervals a≤x<b, a cumulative point at b records the count below b. The booklet wording 'up to and including' should be treated with this boundary convention in mind. Integer scores in unit-width bins have half-integer boundaries.
:::
